steps.title: Launch the Experiential Learning Community
steps.summary: Launch the Experiential Learning Community as the prototype for King's wider Strategic Communities of Practice model. Mobilise growing interest across faculties in developing more experiential and internship-like learning within the curriculum by connecting interested colleagues from faculties and professional services. Hold an informal pre-launch event in July, establish a dedicated Teams space for the emerging community, and formally launch it through an Unconference on 14 September 2026. Use the Unconference to share existing practice, form new connections, surface ideas and potential collaborations, begin a King's Taxonomy of Experiential Learning, agree practical next steps and aspirations for the community's first year, and identify a small group of informal community leads or champions who can help sustain participation and mobilise early activity alongside Mark Peace and King's Academy. These will be voluntary, interim mobilisation roles without a central workload-release entitlement. They will not constitute appointment as a future funded convenor or confer an automatic advantage in a subsequent convenor selection process. Complete this prototype launch phase by the end of September 2026. The experience of forming the community, sustaining participation through Teams and translating the launch into collaborative activity will inform the common model used for subsequent communities.

outputs.title: Founding community mobilised
outputs.summary: A cross-institutional network of faculty and professional-services colleagues brought together through the July pre-launch, wider engagement and the September Unconference.
acceptanceCriteria: The July informal pre-launch event has taken place and helped identify the founding network.
At least 50 people participate in the Unconference, with representation from at least six faculties and multiple professional-services areas.
Careers and Employability and King's Academy contribute visibly to the launch.
A small group of prospective informal leads or champions is identified from across the founding community to help sustain participation and carry activity forward after the launch.

outputs.title: Experiential Learning Unconference launch
outputs.summary: The Strategic Community of Practice formally launched on 14 September 2026 through a participatory Unconference focused on sharing practice, generating ideas, forming connections and identifying opportunities for collaboration.
acceptanceCriteria: The Unconference is delivered on 14 September 2026.
Participant-led discussions, examples and ideas are captured.
The purpose of the community and routes for continued involvement are made clear.
The event creates visible connections between colleagues with related interests and potential collaborations.

outputs.title: Experiential Learning SCoP Teams space
outputs.summary: A shared Teams space through which members can continue exchanging practice, developing ideas, forming collaborations and coordinating the community's activity, including colleagues unable to attend the launch.
acceptanceCriteria: The Teams space is provisioned before the Unconference and founding participants are invited.
At least 40 colleagues have joined by the end of September 2026.
Clear administration and moderation arrangements are in place.
Launch materials, the synthesis map and agreed next steps are published in the space.

outputs.title: Unconference synthesis map
outputs.summary: A visual synthesis of the practices, concepts, relationships and emerging opportunities surfaced during the day, forming the initial basis of a King's Taxonomy of Experiential Learning.
acceptanceCriteria: The principal forms of experiential and internship-like learning surfaced during the day are represented.
Existing examples, shared ideas and potential connections are captured.
Areas requiring further definition or development are identified.
The synthesis map is published through the Teams space.

outputs.title: First-year priorities and informal mobilisation leadership
outputs.summary: An initial set of actionable priorities, potential collaborations and aspirations agreed through the Unconference, together with a small group of informal community leads or champions who will work with Mark Peace and King's Academy to sustain participation and mobilise the community's early activity.
acceptanceCriteria: At least three practical priorities or collaboration strands are identified.
Interested contributors are associated with each strand where possible.
A small and appropriately diverse group of informal leads or champions is identified.
The informal group understands its role in connecting participants, progressing early priorities and helping shape the community’s first year.
The roles are explicitly described as voluntary and interim, without a central workload-release entitlement.
Informal leadership is clearly distinguished from the later open process for funded convenor appointments.
Immediate actions and responsibilities are recorded and shared through the Teams space.

existingCapacity.contribution: Lead community mobilisation, design and convene the July pre-launch and September Unconference, coordinate contributors, and oversee synthesis and follow-through.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The launch would lack clear ownership, coherence and follow-through.

existingCapacity.role: Volunteer event, facilitation and community support
existingCapacity.owner: Careers and Employability and King's Academy
existingCapacity.contribution: Support event design, communications, participant engagement, facilitation, capture of outputs and establishment of the continuing community.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The event would place too much operational demand on the step lead and provide less effective facilitation, capture and follow-through.

existingCapacity.contribution: Contribute examples, ideas and expertise; participate in the Unconference; and help identify the community's priorities, collaboration opportunities and prospective champions.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The launch would not represent the breadth of institutional interest or establish a viable cross-institutional community.

newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before catering is commissioned for 14 September 2026
newInvestment.rationale: Provides a reasonable provisional envelope for refreshments and light catering for up to 100 participants, supporting an inclusive and hospitable participatory event.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The event can still proceed, but the participant experience, dwell time and opportunity for informal community formation may be reduced.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm a suitable venue and event arrangements for an Unconference of up to 100 participants on 14 September 2026.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The formal launch cannot proceed at the intended scale or in the intended participatory format.

enablingConditions.condition: Provision the Experiential Learning SCoP Teams space before the formal launch.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Colleagues unable to attend and participants seeking to continue the work would lack a shared route into the community.

enablingConditions.condition: Secure broad and timely promotion across faculties and professional services.
enablingConditions.owner: Mark Peace with Careers and Employability and King's Academy volunteers
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Attendance and institutional representation may be too narrow to form a credible founding community.

risks.title: Welcome Week timing reduces availability
risks.mitigation: Issue invitations and promotion early, use the July pre-launch to build commitment, and use the Teams space to enable colleagues who cannot attend to join the community, review the synthesis and contribute to next steps. The 14 September date remains preferable to moving into the teaching term or into the pre-holiday and conference period.

risks.title: The launch creates interest but not a continuing community
risks.mitigation: Use a participant-led Unconference format, agree practical next steps and collaboration strands during the event, identify prospective champions, and carry activity forward through the Teams space.

steps.title: Agree the SCoP Operating Model
steps.summary: By December 2026, agree the standard operating model for Strategic Communities of Practice. Define how communities are established and led, how they are resourced, what their funding may be used for, how decisions are made, how they are governed and held to account, and the minimum expectations for activity, outputs and institutional impact. Alongside this, develop an institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for community convenors and colleagues leading funded projects. Faculties will need to take a view on how this can operate consistently and fairly within their own workload and resource arrangements. Use evidence and learning from the Experiential Learning prototype while developing the model, and secure enough clarity to support the first funded convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: Standard SCoP operating model
outputs.summary: A clear and reusable model defining how Strategic Communities of Practice are established, led, supported, operated, reviewed, renewed and, where necessary, closed.
acceptanceCriteria: The model defines the responsibilities of convenors, members, the central support function and the governing committee.
The model sets expectations for participation, communication, collaboration and decision-making.
The relationship between community activity and institutional education priorities is clear.
The model is approved through the agreed senior education governance route by December 2026.

outputs.title: SCoP resourcing and eligible-use framework
outputs.summary: An agreed framework defining the indicative resource available to communities, the balance between convenor support, community activity and funded projects, and the purposes for which SCoP funding may be used.
acceptanceCriteria: The indicative resource envelope and its principal components are defined.
Eligible and ineligible uses of funding are clear, including support for purposeful activity, collaboration, inquiry, dissemination and institutional change.
Budget ownership, authorisation, monitoring and reporting arrangements are documented.
The framework is sufficiently clear to inform the first convenor and community-project calls.

outputs.title: SCoP governance and accountability framework
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with senior education governance sponsor
outputs.summary: A defined route through which communities agree plans and priorities, report on activity and expenditure, demonstrate progress and impact, and receive challenge, support and decisions about continuation or change.
acceptanceCriteria: The Innovation Committee's remit, membership, delegated authority and reporting route are agreed.
The process through which communities agree and report their plans, priorities and expenditure is defined.
Annual review, renewal, escalation and closure arrangements are documented.
The relationship between the Innovation Committee and existing education governance is clear.

outputs.title: Minimum expectations for SCoP activity, output and impact
outputs.summary: A proportionate baseline defining what every Strategic Community of Practice is expected to do and demonstrate while allowing communities to respond differently to their subject matter.
acceptanceCriteria: Minimum expectations cover a visible programme of activity, sustained participation and exchange or development of practice.
Communities are expected to create tangible outputs, recommendations, resources, collaborations or other appropriate products.
Communities are expected to demonstrate evidence of influence on education, policy, practice or institutional decision-making.
A proportionate annual account of activity, learning, expenditure, outputs and impact is required.

outputs.title: Workload-release and backfill proposition
outputs.owner: Mark Peace with faculty education leadership
outputs.summary: A credible institutional proposition for workload release, workload allocation or backfill for SCoP convenors and colleagues leading funded community projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Eligibility, indicative scale and duration of support are defined.
The relationship between central funding, faculty contribution and local workload arrangements is set out.
Approval, recording and review arrangements are defined.
Faculty positions are sufficiently clear to make a credible and equitable offer in the first funded calls, with any wider unresolved workload-policy questions routed separately.

outputs.title: King's Academy ownership and support model
outputs.summary: A phased model through which a named King's Academy Portfolio Lead takes increasing ownership from Mark Peace, supported by permanent portfolio administration and coordination as convenors and projects change.
acceptanceCriteria: A named King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead, or an agreed appointment route, is confirmed.
Responsibilities and decision rights are clear across the Portfolio Lead, Portfolio Coordinator, individual convenors, project leads and the Innovation Committee.
A phased transfer of portfolio ownership from Mark Peace to King's Academy is agreed.
Initial permanent administrative capacity of 0.2 FTE is confirmed, with scaling assumptions for the three- and six-community portfolio.
Initial Portfolio Lead capacity of 0.1 FTE is costed as a recurrent BAU liability, with future increases considered through the formal review steps.

existingCapacity.role: Step owner and substantive design lead
existingCapacity.contribution: Lead the proposition, develop the operating model, convene the institutional discussions, resolve substantive policy choices and secure approval.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The work would lack substantive leadership and a clear route from consultation to an agreed institutional model.

existingCapacity.contribution: Develop and communicate faculty positions on workload allocation, release, backfill, faculty contribution and the local operation of convenor and project roles.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The first calls could make an offer that faculties cannot implement consistently or fairly.

existingCapacity.contribution: Define the resource envelope, eligible expenditure, budget ownership, approval routes, monitoring and reporting arrangements.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The proposed funding model may be unaffordable, difficult to administer or insufficiently controlled.

existingCapacity.contribution: Advise on workable approaches to workload release, workload allocation and backfill for convenors and funded project leads.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The workload proposition may not be implementable through existing employment and faculty processes.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide the decision route for the operating model and establish the Innovation Committee's remit, authority and relationship with existing education governance.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The model and committee could be established without sufficient authority or accountability.

newInvestment.rationale: Provides 0.1 FTE of time-limited project control and coordination through development of the operating model, the first calls and mobilisation of the first funded cycle. This capacity is temporary and does not transfer into business as usual.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The work may remain a series of useful conversations without sufficient coordination, decision tracking and follow-through to implement the model.

newInvestment.item: King's Academy SCoP Project Support Officer and Portfolio Coordinator
newInvestment.rationale: Provides an initial 0.2 FTE of permanent administrative and coordinating capacity in King's Academy. During mobilisation the role supports meetings, records, consultation, communications, calls and process design; in business as usual it maintains committee support, annual processes, records, onboarding, reporting and continuity as convenors change.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Detailed administration would fall to the substantive lead and no permanent operational capacity or institutional memory would be established for the portfolio.

newInvestment.item: King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead workload release or backfill
newInvestment.rationale: Provides an initial 0.1 FTE of protected senior capacity for a named King's Academy colleague to work alongside Mark Peace, take increasing ownership of the SCoP portfolio, support and challenge convenors, maintain strategic coherence and lead review and renewal. The £10,000 annual planning envelope should be recalculated against the named colleague's grade and the agreed release or backfill route.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Permanent ownership would remain with Mark Peace by default or depend on unprotected goodwill, making the model difficult to sustain as convenors change and the portfolio expands.

enablingConditions.condition: King's Academy identifies a prospective SCoP Portfolio Lead and protects approximately 0.1 FTE for design and shadowing during Step 2.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Early in the September-December 2026 design period
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The operating model would be designed without the future institutional owner and the transfer from Mark Peace would be delayed.

enablingConditions.condition: Faculties nominate participants with sufficient authority to develop and communicate positions on workload release, backfill and faculty contribution.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before the workload proposition is finalised
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Consultation may produce views but not positions that can support a credible institutional offer.

enablingConditions.condition: Finance, HR and faculty operations participate early enough to shape the model rather than being asked to approve a completed proposal.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: During the first phase of model design
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Late operational objections could delay approval or require substantial redesign.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm the senior governance route that will approve the operating model and establish the Innovation Committee with sufficient delegated authority.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The model may be agreed informally without an authoritative decision or effective accountability route.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm the funding and release or backfill route for the initial 0.1 FTE King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead capacity.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The transfer of ownership from Mark Peace would begin without protected capacity and could become unsustainable before the first formal review.

risks.title: Faculties do not reach a sufficiently clear workload position
risks.mitigation: Develop a workable proposition for the first calls, record faculty positions and exceptions, and route any wider institutional workload-policy questions separately rather than requiring them to be resolved within this step.

risks.title: Permanent ownership remains with Mark Peace by default
risks.mitigation: Identify the King's Academy Portfolio Lead during Step 2, agree a phased transfer of responsibility and record the associated workload-release or backfill requirement.

risks.title: Permanent administrative capacity is treated as temporary project support
risks.mitigation: Record the initial 0.2 FTE Portfolio Coordinator as recurrent King's Academy capacity from the outset, with explicit assumptions about how it may need to scale as the portfolio grows.

risks.title: The operating model is either too vague or too prescriptive
risks.mitigation: Define firm minimum expectations, decision rights and financial controls while allowing each community flexibility over its substantive programme, outputs and routes to impact.

risks.title: The Innovation Committee is established without sufficient authority
risks.mitigation: Agree its remit, delegated decisions, reporting route and relationship with existing education governance before the operating model is approved.

steps.title: Recognise and mobilise the AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities
steps.summary: During September and October 2026, recognise and connect the informal communities of practice already developing around AI in Education and Inclusive Education. Build from the people, networks, activity and informal leadership already in place rather than replacing or rebranding what is working. Identify a small group of informal leads or champions in each area to work alongside Mark Peace and King's Academy, broaden participation, articulate emerging priorities and help mobilise early activity. These will be voluntary, interim mobilisation roles without a central workload-release entitlement. They will not constitute appointment as future funded convenors or confer an automatic advantage in subsequent convenor selection. By the end of October, connect both communities, together with the Experiential Learning Community launched through Step 1, to the emerging common SCoP operating model and the more sustained community-building work in Step 4.

outputs.title: Existing AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities recognised
outputs.summary: A proportionate, relationship-led picture of the people, networks, activity, communication routes and institutional connections already present in each area, providing a basis for mobilisation without imposing a new structure prematurely.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing networks, forums, communication spaces, regular activity and visible areas of interest are identified for both communities.
Colleagues already providing informal leadership, coordination or connective work are recognised.
Important gaps in faculty, disciplinary, professional-services or other relevant participation are identified.
The mobilisation approach builds from existing identities and activity rather than assuming that every network must be absorbed, renamed or replaced.

outputs.title: Informal mobilisation leadership identified
outputs.summary: A small group of informal leads or champions for AI in Education and for Inclusive Education, able to connect existing participants, broaden involvement, articulate priorities and help mobilise each community alongside the wider SCoP programme.
acceptanceCriteria: A small group of informal leads or champions is identified for each community rather than relying on a single individual where this can reasonably be avoided.
The groups reflect an appropriate breadth of existing activity and institutional participation.
The role is described as voluntary, interim and proportionate, without a central workload-release entitlement.
The role is clearly distinguished from later funded convenor appointments and does not confer an automatic advantage in an open selection process.
The informal leads understand the support available from Mark Peace, the King's Academy Portfolio Lead and the Portfolio Coordinator.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation plans agreed
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with Mark Peace and King's Academy
outputs.summary: A light-touch mobilisation route for each community, connecting existing activity to wider participation and defining practical next steps before the sustained development phase.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community has a clear route through which interested colleagues can join or remain connected.
An appropriate existing or new communication space is identified, with proportionate administration arrangements.
One or more initial priorities, questions or activity strands are agreed for each community.
Immediate actions and informal owners are recorded without creating an unfunded programme of work that exceeds the voluntary nature of the roles.
The handoff into Step 4 is clear, including what should be developed, broadened or tested during the subsequent community-building phase.

outputs.title: Three communities connected within the emerging SCoP frame
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with Mark Peace
outputs.summary: Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education each have identifiable informal mobilisation leadership and a clear relationship with the emerging common operating model, portfolio support and later funded-convenor process.
acceptanceCriteria: The Experiential Learning informal leads established through Step 1 are recognised alongside the equivalent groups for AI in Education and Inclusive Education.
All three communities have a named route into the King's Academy Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator.
The emerging operating model, current support arrangements and expectations for the mobilisation period are communicated consistently across the three communities.
The temporary status of informal leadership and the later open route to funded convenorship are clear.
All three communities are ready to enter the sustained community-building and operating-conventions work in Step 4 by the end of October 2026.

existingCapacity.role: Step sponsor and institutional relationship lead
existingCapacity.contribution: Engage existing networks, recognise informal activity and leadership, connect the communities to the wider programme and support agreement of proportionate mobilisation routes.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The work could become disconnected from the wider SCoP programme or approach existing communities without sufficient institutional context and trust.

existingCapacity.contribution: Use the Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator capacity established through Step 2 to support relationships, meetings, contact records, communication spaces, mobilisation planning and connection to the common operating model.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The communities may be recognised but lack a consistent route into portfolio support, coordination and the shared operating model.

existingCapacity.role: Existing AI in Education and Inclusive Education networks and participants
existingCapacity.owner: Existing community participants and network leads
existingCapacity.contribution: Share existing activity and connections, help identify the current constituency and gaps, and shape a mobilisation approach that strengthens rather than displaces what already works.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The programme could construct an artificial picture of the communities or duplicate and weaken existing activity.

existingCapacity.role: Voluntary informal community leads and champions
existingCapacity.contribution: Connect participants, broaden involvement, articulate early priorities and help mobilise activity within a contained voluntary role alongside Mark Peace and King's Academy.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The communities would lack sufficient distributed leadership and the mobilisation burden would fall back onto the central programme team.

existingCapacity.contribution: Coordinate contacts, meetings, actions, dependencies and the handoff into Step 4 using the temporary capacity already funded through Step 2.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Relationship-led mobilisation may not translate into a clear, coordinated route across both communities and the wider portfolio.

enablingConditions.condition: Existing community participants and network leads are willing to engage in a light-touch recognition and mobilisation process.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The programme may lack the legitimacy and knowledge required to build from existing activity.

enablingConditions.condition: Informal leads accept a proportionate and clearly bounded voluntary role without an expectation of central workload release.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Mobilisation may depend on ambiguous or excessive goodwill and become difficult to sustain.

enablingConditions.condition: Communications consistently distinguish informal mobilisation leadership from the later open process for funded convenor appointments.
enablingConditions.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before informal leads are publicly identified
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Informal recognition could be interpreted as pre-selection, discouraging later applicants and undermining the credibility of the funded call.

risks.title: Formal recognition disrupts activity that already works
risks.mitigation: Begin with listening and recognition, use existing names and networks where appropriate, and avoid imposing a single structure or programme before the communities have helped shape it.

risks.title: Voluntary informal leadership becomes an excessive or open-ended workload
risks.mitigation: Use shared leadership where possible, keep the mobilisation ask contained, provide practical central support and reserve substantive funded accountability for the later convenor appointments.

risks.title: Informal leads are perceived as pre-selected funded convenors
risks.mitigation: State consistently that the roles are interim and voluntary, publish a later open selection route and avoid giving informal leads any automatic status or advantage in that process.

risks.title: Existing communities are narrower than the intended institutional SCoPs
risks.mitigation: Recognise the existing core while identifying gaps in participation, then use the mobilisation plan and Step 4 to broaden the communities without displacing the people who have already built them.

steps.title: Refine the operating model by piloting the first three communities
steps.summary: From January to June 2027, pilot the agreed Strategic Communities of Practice operating model through the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities. Support the three communities to operate under their informal mobilisation leadership, sustain and broaden participation, deliver useful activity and pursue emerging priorities. The pilots will operate from the outset within the governance, accountability, budget-control and escalation arrangements approved through Step 2, with clear decision rights and institutional oversight through King's Academy and the Innovation Committee. Use live operation to test whether the model is practical, proportionate and sufficiently supportive, refining processes, guidance and conventions without reopening the fundamental authority or accountability of the approved governance framework. Capture the evidence and continuity requirements needed to transfer leadership to funded convenors and integrate funded projects from September 2027. Informal leads remain voluntary and interim during this phase and do not assume the full accountability intended for later funded convenors.

outputs.title: Three community pilots operating
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with King's Academy
outputs.summary: Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education each operate as an active pilot community with an identifiable constituency, a clear participation route, functioning informal leadership and sustained communication across the pilot period.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community has a short pilot plan setting out its initial priorities, participation route, indicative activity and relationship to the common operating model.
Each community has an active communication space and a clear route through which interested colleagues can join or remain involved.
Participation extends beyond the informal leads and shows evidence of broadening across relevant faculties, disciplines, professional-services areas or other constituencies.
Informal leadership is shared where possible, remains explicitly voluntary and interim, and is supported rather than replaced by central portfolio capacity.
The three communities remain active throughout the January-June pilot rather than relying on a single launch event or isolated meeting.

outputs.title: Community-led programmes of activity delivered
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with the King's Academy Portfolio Lead
outputs.summary: A proportionate programme in each community that responds to its own priorities while demonstrating the practical value of sustained exchange, collaboration and institutionally connected activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Each community delivers at least two purposeful activities during the pilot period rather than being limited to routine coordination meetings.

Activities may include practice exchange, collaborative inquiry, workshops, resource development, institutional propositions, student involvement, external engagement or connections between related initiatives.
Each community uses its operating allowance to support at least one event, guest speaker, specialist contributor, student group or external partner where this is relevant to its priorities.
Each community produces at least one tangible output, collaboration, recommendation or proposition through its pilot activity.
Activity, participation, expenditure and emerging outputs are recorded proportionately through the shared community and portfolio arrangements.

outputs.title: Governance and accountability demonstrated in practice
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with the Innovation Committee
outputs.summary: The approved governance framework is used consistently across the three pilots, providing visible institutional authority, oversight and financial control while preserving appropriate community autonomy.
acceptanceCriteria: The Innovation Committee or agreed governing forum is operational and understands its delegated authority before the pilots begin.
Decision rights are clear across informal community leads, the King's Academy Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator, Mark Peace and the governing forum.
Each community has a clear route for advice, approval, escalation and influence on institutional education policy or practice.
Budget ownership, delegated approval, expenditure records and material commitments are managed consistently across all three communities.
Each community provides an approved pilot plan and budget, a light-touch midpoint update and an end-of-pilot account covering participation, activity, expenditure, outputs, risks and emerging impact.
Material decisions, exceptions and unresolved risks are recorded and routed through the agreed governance arrangements.
The governance arrangements are judged sufficiently robust to support funded convenors and community-aligned projects from September 2027.

outputs.title: Operating model refined through pilot evidence
outputs.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with Mark Peace
outputs.summary: An evidence-led refinement of the common operating model that confirms the institutional controls that must remain consistent, improves practical processes and identifies where communities should retain flexibility.
acceptanceCriteria: The pilot synthesis distinguishes elements of governance, accountability, delegated authority, budget control, reporting, escalation and review that remain fixed across all communities.
Practical guidance is refined for participation, onboarding, communication, shared leadership, priority-setting, collaborative activity, evidence collection and routes into institutional influence.
Differences between the three communities are used to identify where standardisation would be unhelpful or disproportionate.
The actual demand placed on informal leads, the Portfolio Lead, the Portfolio Coordinator and temporary project-management capacity is assessed.
The adequacy and eligible use of the base community activity allowance are assessed against actual pilot activity and outcomes.

The Innovation Committee formally receives the pilot synthesis, approves refinements within its authority and escalates any material governance or resource changes through the agreed senior education route.

outputs.title: Transition packs for funded convenors and projects
outputs.owner: Informal community leads with the King's Academy Portfolio Coordinator
outputs.summary: A proportionate handover position for each community so that funded convenors and project teams can inherit and strengthen established relationships and activity rather than restarting the communities in September 2027.
acceptanceCriteria: Each transition pack records the community constituency, participation routes, active relationships, current priorities, work underway and commitments already made.
The expectations community members have of the funded convenor and the support required from the portfolio team are captured.
Outputs, propositions or collaborations requiring continuity into the funded cycle are identified.
Leadership-transition risks and sensitivities are recorded, including how informal leads will remain involved without being treated as pre-selected or displaced.
The packs are available in time to inform Step 6 appointment, mobilisation and handover arrangements.

existingCapacity.contribution: Maintain strategic coherence, support the informal leads, resolve substantive questions and ensure pilot learning informs the wider SCoP model and funded transition.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The pilots may generate activity without a coherent route into operating-model refinement or wider institutional priorities.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide visible institutional ownership, support and challenge the communities, operate the approved governance arrangements and lead the portfolio-level synthesis and refinement.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Governance confidence and portfolio coherence would depend excessively on Mark Peace and the model would not demonstrate sustainable institutional ownership.

existingCapacity.contribution: Support communications, community spaces, meetings, events, budget records, participation evidence, governance papers and transition packs using the recurrent capacity funded through Step 2.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Operational and reporting work would fall onto voluntary informal leads or substantive leadership, weakening both participation and control.

existingCapacity.contribution: Coordinate the three pilots, maintain actions, dependencies and evidence, and support the refinement and handover work using the temporary capacity funded through Step 2.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The three pilots may proceed inconsistently and fail to produce a coherent evidence base or timely transition.

existingCapacity.contribution: Shape priorities, connect participants, host or enable activity, advise on the operating model and prepare continuity for funded leadership within a shared, bounded and supported voluntary role.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The pilots would lack community legitimacy and distributed leadership; if the role is insufficiently bounded, informal leads may become unfunded substitutes for later convenors.

existingCapacity.role: Community members, students and institutional or external partners
existingCapacity.contribution: Contribute practice, expertise, challenge, activity and collaboration so that the model is tested through meaningful community work rather than central process alone.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The pilots would test administration rather than the ability of communities to create useful exchange, collaboration and institutional influence.

newInvestment.item: Base community activity and engagement allowance
newInvestment.periodNeeded: From January 2027 onward; £6,000 for the January-June 2027 pilot and £12,000 per full academic year thereafter
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before January 2027 pilot activity is commissioned
newInvestment.rationale: Establishes a minimum viable recurrent operating allowance of £4,000 per community per full academic year, pro-rated to £2,000 per community for the six-month pilot. It enables guest speakers, modest events and hospitality, facilitation, materials, communications, student participation, accessibility costs and limited specialist or partner contributions. It is separate from convenor workload release, permanent staffing and substantive funded projects, which are added through later steps.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The communities could still meet, but visible activity would depend on goodwill and uneven local budgets, reducing participation, credibility and the reliability of evidence about the operating model.

enablingConditions.condition: The SCoP governance and accountability framework is approved, the governing forum is operational and delegated authority is communicated before the pilots begin.
enablingConditions.owner: King's Academy Portfolio Lead with the senior education governance sponsor
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Pilot language could be interpreted as permission to improvise governance, weakening institutional confidence and financial control.

enablingConditions.condition: King's Academy is confirmed as budget holder and implements proportionate approval, recording, monitoring and year-end treatment for community operating allowances.
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before the pilot allowances are released
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Communities may have nominal funding without a workable or controlled route to spend it.

enablingConditions.condition: Informal leaders agree a bounded voluntary role and central support is available for administration, communications, events, budget records and reporting.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The pilot may depend on excessive goodwill or turn informal leadership into an unfunded substitute for convenorship.

risks.title: Pilot language undermines confidence in institutional governance
risks.mitigation: Communicate that the governance and accountability framework has already been approved and that the pilot tests practical operation and proportionality, not whether governance is required. Keep decision rights, reporting, budget control and escalation visible throughout.

risks.title: Informal leads become de facto unfunded convenors
risks.mitigation: Keep the role shared, voluntary, interim and bounded; place administration and formal budget control with the portfolio team; and reserve substantive accountability and workload support for the funded appointments.

risks.title: A common operating model over-standardises different communities
risks.mitigation: Separate fixed institutional controls from flexible community practices and use evidence from all three pilots to identify where variation is necessary and productive.

risks.title: The recurrent activity allowance becomes an untested entitlement
risks.mitigation: Treat £4,000 per community as a planning assumption, review its adequacy and use through the pilot, and base later portfolio scaling on evidence while preserving the initial £12,000 annual BAU liability unless formally revised.

risks.title: Activity is visible but produces weak learning or continuity
risks.mitigation: Use agreed pilot plans, midpoint updates, proportionate evidence and transition packs so that activity informs operating-model refinement and the September 2027 funded handover.

steps.title: Run the first funded convenor and community-project calls
steps.summary: From January to April 2027, run coordinated calls for funded Community Convenors and community-aligned projects. Complete assessment and selection by April so that successful convenors, faculty release and backfill arrangements, project leads and funding can be confirmed and mobilised for a September start.

outputs.title: Completed institutional calls
outputs.summary: Convenors and projects selected through clear eligibility, support, assessment and decision arrangements.

outputs.title: Selected funded leadership and project portfolio
outputs.summary: Successful convenors and projects identified for appointment and commencement in September 2027.

steps.title: Confirm appointments and mobilise the first funded cycle
steps.summary: From May to August 2027, confirm the selected convenors and projects, finalise faculty release, workload allocation, backfill, budgets and delivery arrangements, and manage the handover from interim leadership. Prepare the three communities, funded convenors and project teams to begin the first funded operating cycle in September.

outputs.title: Confirmed funded appointments and projects
outputs.summary: Convenors, project leads, budgets, workload arrangements and expectations confirmed for September commencement.

outputs.title: First funded cycle ready to operate
outputs.summary: The three communities and their funded activity are mobilised for the 2027-28 academic year.

steps.title: Review the initial mobilisation, agree the expansion portfolio and launch the 2028-29 calls
steps.summary: During July and August 2027, review and report on the initial community-building phase as soon as it concludes. Assess establishment, participation, governance, interim convenorship, faculty support, project mechanisms and emerging institutional influence; refine the model; agree the three additional strategic communities to be developed for 2028-29; and launch the associated convenor and community-project calls by the end of August. As part of the review, assess the workload required for King's Academy portfolio leadership and administration and decide whether to release the planned additional capacity for the first funded three-community cycle.

outputs.title: Initial mobilisation review
outputs.summary: An evidence-led assessment of whether the first three communities and their shared operating model have been successfully established.

outputs.title: Approved six-community portfolio
outputs.summary: Three additional strategic communities agreed for development and funded operation in the 2028-29 academic year.

outputs.title: Open 2028-29 convenor and project calls
outputs.summary: Calls launched by the end of August for renewed and new convenors and community-aligned projects across the approved six-community portfolio.

outputs.title: Support capacity agreed for the first funded cycle
outputs.summary: An evidence-based decision on whether to increase permanent portfolio leadership and coordination capacity for the first funded three-community cycle.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual leadership and administrative workload from initial mobilisation is reviewed.
The need for the planned increase to 0.2 FTE Portfolio Lead and 0.4 FTE Portfolio Coordinator capacity is confirmed, amended or declined.
Any approved incremental recurrent funding is in place for September 2027.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead capacity for the three-community cycle
newInvestment.rationale: Adds 0.1 FTE of recurrent Portfolio Lead capacity, taking the role from 0.1 to 0.2 FTE if the initial mobilisation review confirms that this is required to own and support the first funded three-community cycle.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The Portfolio Lead may not have sufficient protected capacity to support convenors, maintain coherence and lead the annual portfolio cycle.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Coordinator capacity for the three-community cycle
newInvestment.rationale: Adds 0.2 FTE of recurrent portfolio coordination, taking the role from 0.2 to 0.4 FTE if the review confirms that this is required to administer the first funded three-community cycle.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Annual calls, committee support, onboarding, reporting and portfolio records may exceed the capacity established during mobilisation.

steps.title: Operate the first funded three-community cycle
steps.summary: Operate the Experiential Learning, AI in Education and Inclusive Education communities through the September 2027-June 2028 academic-year cycle. Support their funded convenors, programmes, projects, participation and routes into institutional influence while gathering consistent evidence of activity, outcomes and resource requirements.

outputs.title: First funded operating cycle
outputs.summary: Three communities complete a coherent September-June cycle with funded leadership, visible activity and evidence of their contribution.

steps.title: Complete selection for the expanded portfolio
steps.summary: During September and October 2027, assess the 2028-29 convenor and community-project calls launched following the initial mobilisation review. Complete selection by the end of October, covering renewals, new appointments and the three additional communities, so that the expanded portfolio can move directly into mobilisation from November.

outputs.title: Selected 2028-29 convenors and projects
outputs.summary: Renewed and new convenors and a funded project portfolio selected for the six-community operating cycle beginning in September 2028.

steps.title: Mobilise the expanded six-community portfolio
steps.summary: From November 2027 to August 2028, confirm appointments, faculty release, workload allocation, backfill, budgets and project delivery arrangements. Establish the three additional communities, build their founding memberships and priorities, and prepare all six communities, convenors and funded projects to begin the next operating cycle together in September.

outputs.title: Expanded portfolio ready to operate
outputs.summary: All six communities, their funded convenors and their selected projects are mobilised for September 2028.

steps.title: Review the first funded operating cycle, refine the model and launch the 2029-30 calls
steps.summary: During July and August 2028, review and report on the completed September-June operating cycle. Assess participation, activity, impact, governance, convenorship, faculty release and backfill, funding, project mechanisms and institutional influence; refine the model for the expanded portfolio; and launch the 2029-30 convenor and community-project calls by the end of August. As part of the review, assess the workload required for the expanded six-community portfolio and decide whether to release the final planned increments in permanent King's Academy leadership and administration.

outputs.title: First funded-cycle impact and operating-model review
outputs.summary: An assessment of the first funded cycle with agreed refinements to governance, resourcing and operating arrangements for the expanded portfolio.

outputs.title: Open 2029-30 convenor and project calls
outputs.summary: Calls launched by the end of August for the next annual portfolio of convenors and community-aligned projects.

outputs.title: Support capacity agreed for the six-community portfolio
outputs.summary: An evidence-based decision on whether to increase permanent portfolio leadership and coordination capacity for the expanded six-community portfolio.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual workload from the first funded three-community cycle is reviewed.
The need for the planned increase to 0.3 FTE Portfolio Lead and 0.6 FTE Portfolio Coordinator capacity is confirmed, amended or declined.
Any approved incremental recurrent funding is in place for September 2028.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Lead capacity for the six-community portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Adds a further 0.1 FTE of recurrent Portfolio Lead capacity, taking the role from 0.2 to 0.3 FTE if the funded-cycle review confirms that this is required for the six-community portfolio.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Strategic oversight, convenor support and cross-community learning may become too thin as the portfolio doubles in size.

newInvestment.item: Additional King's Academy SCoP Portfolio Coordinator capacity for the six-community portfolio
newInvestment.rationale: Adds a further 0.2 FTE of recurrent portfolio coordination, taking the role from 0.4 to 0.6 FTE if the review confirms that this is required to administer the six-community portfolio.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The expanded annual cycle, committee workload, records, reporting and convenor handovers may not be administered reliably.

steps.title: Operate the six-community portfolio
steps.summary: Operate all six strategic communities through the September 2028-June 2029 academic-year cycle, supporting their funded convenors, programmes, projects, institutional influence and cross-community learning while gathering consistent evidence of participation, outcomes and resource requirements.

outputs.title: Full six-community operating cycle
outputs.summary: Six communities complete a coherent September-June cycle, including the contribution of their funded projects.

steps.title: Complete 2029-30 selection and develop the BAU settlement
steps.summary: During September and October 2028, assess the 2029-30 convenor and community-project calls and complete selection by the end of October for a September start. In parallel, develop the proposed permanent institutional ownership, governance route, budget holding, recurrent resource settlement and annual planning arrangements required for business as usual.

outputs.title: Selected 2029-30 portfolio
outputs.summary: Convenors and projects selected for the operating cycle beginning in September 2029.

outputs.title: Proposed BAU resource and governance settlement
outputs.summary: A developed proposal for permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and the continuing annual commissioning rhythm.

steps.title: Mobilise the 2029-30 portfolio and prepare the institutional handover
steps.summary: From November 2028 to August 2029, confirm appointments, faculty release, backfill, budgets and project delivery arrangements for the 2029-30 portfolio. Prepare the transfer of governance, reporting, operational support, budgets and accountability from mobilisation to the proposed permanent institutional owner.

outputs.title: Portfolio mobilised and handover prepared
outputs.summary: The next annual portfolio is mobilised for September and the operational, governance and resource arrangements are ready to transfer once the permanent model is approved in August.

steps.title: Review the six-community cycle and confirm the permanent model
steps.summary: During July and August 2029, review and report on the completed six-community operating cycle. Assess impact and sustainability, determine which communities should continue or evolve, and approve the permanent institutional owner, governance arrangements, recurrent resource settlement and annual planning cycle by the end of August. Use evidence from the operating cycles to confirm or adjust the cumulative recurrent King's Academy portfolio leadership and administration settlement, without counting investment already introduced through earlier steps a second time.

outputs.title: Six-community impact and sustainability review
outputs.summary: A completed assessment of the expanded portfolio and its contribution after a full operating cycle.

outputs.title: Approved permanent institutional model
outputs.summary: Permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and the annual commissioning and operating rhythm confirmed by the end of August 2029.

outputs.title: Confirmed permanent SCoP support settlement
outputs.owner: King's Academy with the agreed governance route
outputs.summary: The final recurrent leadership and administrative capacity for the permanent SCoP portfolio, confirmed or amended using evidence from mobilisation and funded operating cycles.
acceptanceCriteria: The final Portfolio Lead and Portfolio Coordinator workload assumptions are agreed from evidence of actual demand.
Grades or backfill routes, recurrent costs, institutional owner and budget holder are confirmed.
The settlement explicitly recognises the recurrent liabilities introduced in Steps 2, 7 and 11 and does not count them again as new investment.

steps.title: Transition to business as usual
steps.summary: From September 2029, complete the transfer to the permanent institutional owner so that Strategic Communities of Practice continue through the established rhythm of September-June operation, July-August review, reporting and call launch, September-October selection and November-August mobilisation.

outputs.title: Business-as-usual transition complete
outputs.summary: Strategic Communities of Practice operate through permanent ownership, governance, recurrent resources and an established annual planning cycle from September 2029.
